text:
alex: anyone else seeing a spike in internal DNS timeouts from GPU nodes? multiple embedder pods returning 502s

maria: yeah started ~05:10 UTC, node-local-dns returning SERVFAIL a lot

alex: sample from pod logs:
```
ERROR calling core-service: lookup core-service.default.svc.cluster.local: server misbehaving
... retries exhausted
```

tj: can you paste a quick `dig` from one of the affected gpu pods? also which pool/region?

alex: running in us-west2 GPU pool; dig output shows SERVFAIL
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short core-service.default.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.1
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 3456
```

sam: tcpdump from the node shows a lot of large UDP fragments getting truncated around same time
```
12:45:03.123456 IP gpu-node0.12345 > coredns.53: UDP, length 1452
12:45:03.123457 IP gpu-node0.12345 > coredns.53: UDP, length 1234 (truncated)
```

karen: we rolled out an MTU clamp to 9000 on the gpu pool host interfaces yesterday for RDMA testing — could be fragmentation + UDP = DNS fails

alex: that tracks. DNS over UDP doesn't like fragmentation; coreDNS might drop truncated packets leading to SERVFAIL

infra-bot: ALERT: core-dns latency > 300ms in us-west2-gpu-pool (5m average)

maria: quick mitigation idea: force node-local-dns to prefer TCP for queries to coreDNS (flip to `TCPOnly` or use short timeout) or clamp UDP MTU lower as a stopgap

sam: quick patch we can try on a canary node: clamp MSS on host so packet sizes don't fragment: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` (apply to the two canary nodes first)

alex: testing `dig +tcp` from pod now... `dig +tcp core-service.default.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.1` appears to succeed

tj: good sign. I'll spin up two nodes in the gpu pool without MTU 9000 and run a 12h soak of internal traffic, plus run `iperf -u` to simulate UDP frag patterns

karen: longer term we should either: 1) ensure path MTU discovery works with RDMA changes, 2) avoid large UDP DNS payloads (enable EDNS size tweaks), or 3) turn on TCP fallback in node-local-dns config

maria: opening an infra ticket with logs, tcpdumps, and the canary plan. assigning to @tj and @sam. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: applying canary iptables now on gpu-node-canary-1, will report if 502s stop

sam: if canary looks good we can roll a daemonset that clamps MTU for DNS traffic only, non-disruptive

alex: update in 10m — initial tests show error rate dropping after iptables clamp (prelim). thanks folks
